resources.string: Apical band share of an acinar cell profile
Band depth from the lumen edge
Band area in the drawing: %1$s u²
At band depth d, the drawing is w = 2 + (6 − 2) × d / 6 units wide. Band area = d × (2 + w) / 2. Band share = 100 × band area / 24, as a percentage of the whole profile.

A pancreatic acinar cell tapers toward a small shared lumen. Secretory granules gather near that apical end, while the nucleus lies toward the broader base. The side-on drawing is a trapezoid 6 drawing units (u) tall, 2 u wide at the lumen and 6 u wide at the base. A shaded band starts at the lumen edge and extends inward. Its area is a property of the invented drawing, not a real cell measurement, granule count, or estimate of secretion.
